Personally, not only am I going to participate in the exchange, but I also think that completely abandoning reddit is the complete wrong way to go about it. I think that reddit and voat can exist at the same time equally. And while I do believe that reddit has many problems, just leaving won't fix them. However, you can do these things to fix some common problems I have encountered:

Shadowbanned

If you've been shadowbanned from reddit unjustifyedly, there are a couple reasons why. The first reason, is that reddit is a huge site. Just look at /r/thebutton. Over 900000 participants. Even more who haven't clicked, and even more who haven't even joined. Reddit is ginormous, and errors are bound to happen. It's also entirely possible that it was your fault. People make mistakes. Either way, just make a new account, under a new name, and don't make the same mistakes twice.

Toxic Community

If a community on a certain community is toxic, you have 3 options: Leave the sub completely(nobody wants to do this), be the better man/woman and don't comment/argue(hard but worth it) or be immature and argue with everyone who has a differing opinion. If a user is seeking you out, make a new account.

I'll update this list as I go with more problems, but for now, this is a good start.
My thoughts on the whole Voat vs. Reddit discussion

Perhaps the issue is not about fixing Reddit, but an understanding it is too far gone to be saved. Through the past year (and even before that according to some interpretations) there has been a persistent strengthening of the grip on the speech there to reorient views as opposed to express them.

Your answer to shadow banning is persisting through newer and newer accounts. I don't really see that as a solution especially if you have to check if you are shadowbanned on a regular basis. I also don't buy that a shadow ban is a mistake as opposed to an abuse of power. Someone has to go out of their way to ban someone, this is a very deliberate action. They felt your opinion unnecessary. Also, your 'don't make the same mistakes twice' assumes one thing: you made a mistake in the first place. On top of this, shadowbanning is a covert way of silencing opinion without someone noticing. I find this underhanded approach worse than a straight ban as it keeps the illusion of open mindedness.

Running from a sub because it is toxic would be fine if it wasn't common place to see brigading occur. Again we imply that arguing is wrong for some reason. Dissent is a healthy part of discussion or else every board becomes a glorified /r/circlejerk without the jokes. Especially when dissent is backed up with statistics, reasoning, sources or other material, which you do see on occasion and you learn something.

Reddit and Voat can exist at the same time sure. I just do not expect it to improve as I see those in power abusing it more and more frequently with transparency going out the door.
